newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest says Austrian east derivatives no threat.
newsitem.headline: Budapest says Austrian east derivatives no threat.

text.p: The Austrian Futures and Options Exchange (OTOB) has little chance of becoming the dominant stage for derivatives trade in central eastern European stocks, the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Friday.

"(OTOB) will not be able to manage its comparative disadvantages," BSE Managing Director Jozsef Rotyis told a news conference. "The large weakness of (OTOB's) ideas is that they do not have the support of the regions' bourses behind them," Rotyis said.
Both OTOB and the BSE plan to launch this year derivative products based upon central eastern European stock indices.
Such products are as yet not traded anywhere.

OTOB surprised the BSE last June when it announced at an international conference held in Budapest that it would launch its own regional derivatives indices for Hungary, Poland, the Czech Republic and Slovakia.
Rotyis said that according to his information, OTOB planned to introduce early this year futures and options products based upon these indices, published since the middle of 1996.

The BSE would also like to build derivative trade later this year on the CESI Central European Share Index, which in cooperation with bourses in the region reflects trends of 73 shares on the Budapest, Prague, Warsaw, Bratislava and Ljubljana bourses.
The CESI index first appeared on February 1 last year.

The Austrian market's relatively small participation in the trade of central eastern European shares and its distance from the underlying markets diminishes OTOB's chances of building a substantial derivatives market on these stocks, Rotyis said. @
Only some one percent of trading in Hungarian shares takes place in Vienna, compared with about 50 percent on London's SEAQ market, he said.
"I would see it as a much larger threat if London launched such a (derivatives) product," Rotyis added.
